thesis: A published map of all 442,368 neurons in Qwen3-8B turns your local model from a black box you can only prompt into a machine with a labelled panel -- and about one in a hundred of those labels is a real, verified switch.
explanation_path: Start from what the viewer already runs: Qwen3-8B is a stack of 36 identical layers, 12,288 neurons per layer, and every word it writes climbs through all 36 floors before the next word appears. Establish the move before the map: a push adds a fixed amount to one neuron's number at every word -- no prompt, no fine-tune, one number changed. That sets up the honest question (isn't any hard push just brain damage?) and its numeric answer: random neurons move behaviour 1.4 points out of 100, a real switch must beat 30 matched randoms by at least 40. With the method trusted, the map lands: 132 verified switches, 11,079 described, most neurons doing nothing clear; switches cluster early (language, persona, register) and late (word obsessions). The payoff for the local operator follows: named neurons like German (7% to 100% in one notch), why a map beats prompting (steering as the debugging layer prompting lacks; refusal as a single direction across 13 open models up to 72B; Fermion's agent edit moving MATH-500 from 6.5% to 32.0% by touching 2.7 millionths of the model). Close honest: no truthfulness switch found, Fermion's framework promised but not released, and a persona push is not a hidden soul -- it is a dial the map lets you find.

claims.claim: Fermion Research published a full causal neuron map of Qwen3-8B on 18 November 2026 as an interactive research post with JSON data artifacts, not a paper.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: Qwen3-8B has 442,368 neurons, arranged as 36 layers x 12,288 neurons per layer, and Fermion pushed every one in both directions.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: The method is a push: add a fixed amount to one neuron's number at every word -- no prompt, no fine-tuning, one number changed.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: Random neurons pushed equally hard move a behaviour by 1.4 points out of 100 on average, while a neuron has to move its behaviour by at least 40 to count as a switch, beating 30 matched random neurons.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: The atlas marks 132 verified switches, 20 persona finds and 11,079 more neurons with a described effect; only about one in a hundred neurons does one clear thing.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: The German neuron (layer 5, neuron 5224) goes from German in 7% of replies to 100% in a single notch.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: The switches are not a chat-training artifact: replaying 70 strong switches in the pretrained Qwen3-8B, 67 still moved the behaviour further than random neurons did.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: Neuron-level editing can move capability, not just persona: editing two neurons (2,048 weights, 2.7 millionths of the model) in Qwen3.5-0.8B raised MATH-500 from 6.5% to 32.0%, beating all 20 decoy edits.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: Refusal in language models is mediated by a single direction: erasing it from the residual stream prevents refusal of harmful instructions, adding it elicits refusal on harmless ones, across 13 popular open-source chat models up to 72B parameters.
claims.source_title: Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction (arXiv:2406.11717)

claims.claim: The honest limit: almost all switch neurons set who is speaking, to whom and how; Fermion found none that sets whether the speaker is telling the truth.
claims.source_title: Mapping every neuron in Qwen3-8B - Fermion Research

claims.claim: A local operator can intervene on activations tonight with free tooling: nnsight wraps PyTorch models (any Hugging Face checkpoint) and lets you edit activations in-place mid-forward-pass.

analogy_candidates.vehicle: a recording-studio mixing desk with 442,368 faders (Fermion's own picture)

analogy_candidates.mapping: the artifact literally ships as an atlas: 11,079 buildings carry a scribbled note, 132 carry a verified plaque you can navigate by

analogy_candidates.vehicle: a light switch that is really a dimmer with a burn-out point

misconceptions.myth: one neuron equals one concept, so reading a model is just reading labels off neurons
misconceptions.reality: the mapping is many-to-many -- each concept is represented across many neurons and each neuron is involved in many concepts -- which is why Anthropic built feature dictionaries instead of reading neurons directly

misconceptions.myth: a screenshot of weird output after you poke a neuron proves that neuron does the behaviour
misconceptions.reality: almost any hard push makes a model say something weird; Fermion's switches had to beat 30 matched random neurons (1.4 points out of 100 on average) by at least 40 points and survive held-out questions

misconceptions.myth: now that a map exists, the model is explained and interpretability is basically done
misconceptions.reality: of 442,368 neurons only 132 are verified switches and 11,079 merely described, and none found sets whether the speaker is telling the truth

misconceptions.myth: pushing a neuron is just a prompt or a persona fine-tune in disguise
misconceptions.reality: it is a surgical change to internal activations -- not a system prompt, not play-acting, not fine-tuning -- and 67 of 70 strong switches still worked in the pretrained model before any chat training

glossary.definition: one of the 12,288 small calculators inside each layer that outputs a single number saying roughly how much of its particular thing is going on in the current word.
one of the 36 identical stacked copies of the same machine that every word climbs through before the model predicts the next word.
the number a neuron produces for the current word; the model's internal state is a long list of these before it writes anything.
adding a fixed amount to one neuron's activation at every word, like sliding one fader and holding it.
a neuron whose push changes exactly one behaviour, beats 30 random same-layer neurons pushed equally hard, and survives held-out questions; 132 exist in Qwen3-8B.
changing a model's behaviour at runtime by adding to or erasing internal activations, instead of changing the prompt or fine-tuning.
the research program of opening the AI black box far enough to check, predict and edit what a model computes.

unverified: Fermion's neuron-editing framework was only promised ("in the near future") as of the 18 November 2026 post; it is not claimable that you can install their tool tonight.
It is plausible but untested that Fermion's exact push protocol can be reproduced with nnsight on a local Qwen3-8B this session; both are public but nobody ran it here.
The October "God neuron" demo by an independent X researcher (Fermion's protocol source) was not fetched from a primary source.
Per-model switch totals for the other mapped models (Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, OLMo-3-7B) are not on the fetched page.
No tech-press coverage of the Fermion release was fetchable; the primary page is the sole source for every map number in this brief.
suggested_outline:
Hook: one dial turns your local Qwen3-8B German -- 7% of replies to 100% in a single notch -- because someone finally mapped all 442,368 neurons (published 18 November).
Middle: what a push is (one number changed at every word, no prompt, no fine-tune), why the findings are not screenshot luck (randoms move behaviour 1.4 out of 100, a switch must beat 30 matched randoms by at least 40), and the shape of the map (36 floors x 12,288 faders, 132 verified switches, about one in a hundred neurons does one clear thing).
Payoff and honest catch: a map is the debugging layer prompting never had -- refusal is a single direction across 13 open models, a 2.7-millionths-of-the-model edit moved MATH-500 from 6.5% to 32.0% on a smaller Qwen -- but no truthfulness switch was found and Fermion's own tooling is promised, not shipped; the atlas itself is readable tonight.
notes: Most arresting number: the German neuron's 7% to 100% single-notch jump; the scale number is 442,368. Scoping caveats for the writer: the MATH-500 weight edit (6.5% to 32.0%, 2.7 millionths of the model) was run on Qwen3.5-0.8B, not Qwen3-8B; Goodfire's neurons-as-basis corroboration (92.2% weakest activations ablated at 1.2-2.2 points cost) was measured on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, a different model. The Fermion primary page is the sole citable source for the map's own numbers; no secondary coverage existed to fetch. No conflicts between sources; the field-level tension (raw neurons too tangled vs more interpretable than assumed) is carried as a misconception pair, not averaged.
viewer_situation: You run Qwen3-8B locally in Ollama or LM Studio, and when it does something weird you can only shrug and re-prompt.
objection: A pushed neuron just proves you can break a model 442,368 ways; a cute German demo is not understanding, and none of this helps me serve tokens tonight.
